proposed_record.reviewerRationale: Coverage value: AIM Defence gains updated ownership, operating context, current activity, a deeper Fractl capability, three program participations and three funding events anchored to the 2024 Canadian Sandbox, 2026 Mission Syracuse and September 2026 selection. Evidence: 19 durable sources from the Department of National Defence, ISED, Australian Defence, Corporations Canada, the Australian Business Register, AusTender and AIM Defence separate observed trials, supplier claims and future integration. Mission/Public Need read: Existing Mission and Public Need relationships remain unchanged; Fractl's directed-energy, precision-tracking and layered counter-UAS premise is clearer, but no current Mission Area warrants a new match. Unknowns: The cross-border ownership tree, configuration lineage, production rate, customer identities, fielding, exact Canadian manufacturing scope and 2026 Sandbox outcomes remain unresolved. Reviewer action: Compare the revised ownership, capability maturity and program participation operations against the legal-identity warning and Canadian/Australian proof boundaries before acceptance.
reviewWarnings: The public AIM Defence brand spans Australian, Canadian and UK entities, but reviewed filings do not establish the legal parent-subsidiary chain or which entity holds Fractl IP, contracts and Canadian staff.

Australia's AIM DEFENCE business-name registration ended August 9, 2026 while the website remained active; current Canadian AIM Defence Inc. is corporation 1782284-7 and the former Canadian namesake is now AIM Kernel Inc.

Public Fractl labels and specifications vary by date and configuration: Fractl:1, Tactical, Civil, less than 100 versus less than 120 kilograms, and demonstrated or reported engagement ranges from 500 metres to 1.5 kilometres.

The 2024 Canadian and Australian trials support bounded prototype performance; they do not establish universal range, weather performance, certified swarm defeat, formal acceptance, operational fielding or combat use.

Mission Syracuse funds production, integration and demonstration toward combat readiness; Australian officials explicitly reserve later LAND 156 procurement and entry into service for a separate program decision.
The 2026 Canadian Counter-UAS Sandbox is scheduled for September 14 to October 9, 2026 and has not begun; no result, prize, procurement consequence or completed integration can yet be claimed.
AIM's operationally proven and sold-on-three-continents language is not supported by disclosed customer names, quantities, acceptance dates or operational-use records in the reviewed sources.
Exact laser power, sensor suite, C2 protocols, weather limits, crew, battery capacity, sustainment, production rate, current lead time and Canadian manufacturing scope remain undisclosed.

after.name: Fractl high-power laser counter-UAS system
after.summary: A remotely operated high-power-laser counter-UAS system combining precision tracking with integrated targeting, cooling, power and laser-safety subsystems to physically disable small uncrewed aircraft. Public trial results are configuration- and condition-specific rather than universal specifications.
features: Precision target tracking and high-power laser hard-kill engagement
Integrated tracking, targeting, cooling, power and laser-safety subsystems
Remote operation through a handheld console
Battery operation or continuous direct-power operation
applications: Point defence of personnel and critical assets
after.maturity: DND reports that the Fractl:1 configuration tracked and neutralized drones at up to 1.5 kilometres and engaged more than 30 drones during the 2024 Sandbox; Australian Defence separately observed a 500-metre hard kill. Mission Syracuse now funds further production, integration and demonstration, while procurement, fielding and in-service acceptance remain separate future decisions.
after.commercialAvailability: AIM markets Fractl in Tactical and Civil variants and the 2025 Australian Defence Export Catalogue describes it as manufactured to order. Current lead time, production rate, customer identities, delivery quantities and configuration-specific acceptance are not public.

proposed_record.executiveRelevanceSummary: AIM Defence brings independently observed high-power-laser counter-UAS demonstrations, Canadian trial participation and Australian transition funding into one compact Fractl product family. The public record supports a 500-metre Australian hard kill and DND-reported Canadian engagements to 1.5 kilometres, but not fielding, universal performance, production rate or completed LAND 156 integration. A first conversation should reconcile the legal entity, current configuration, safety and power envelope, Canadian delivery role and evidence required for acceptance in a layered counter-UAS system.

candidateChanges.reviewer_rationale: Coverage value: AIM Defence gains updated ownership, operating context, current activity, a deeper Fractl capability, three program participations and three funding events anchored to the 2024 Canadian Sandbox, 2026 Mission Syracuse and September 2026 selection. Evidence: 19 durable sources from the Department of National Defence, ISED, Australian Defence, Corporations Canada, the Australian Business Register, AusTender and AIM Defence separate observed trials, supplier claims and future integration. Mission/Public Need read: Existing Mission and Public Need relationships remain unchanged; Fractl's directed-energy, precision-tracking and layered counter-UAS premise is clearer, but no current Mission Area warrants a new match. Unknowns: The cross-border ownership tree, configuration lineage, production rate, customer identities, fielding, exact Canadian manufacturing scope and 2026 Sandbox outcomes remain unresolved. Reviewer action: Compare the revised ownership, capability maturity and program participation operations against the legal-identity warning and Canadian/Australian proof boundaries before acceptance.
